summary: Preinstall hook downloads Bun runtime and executes a heavily obfuscated 727 KB bundle
details: Package @umacloud/cli-linux-musl-arm64 advertises itself as a prebuilt binary artifact for Linux aarch64/musl, but its package.json declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that fetches the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ at install time, marks it executable, and then invokes the shipped 727 KB math_init.js under Bun via execFileSync. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are heavily obfuscated in obfuscator.io style: setup.mjs uses hex identifier renaming (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and per-call proxy wrappers around trivial operations, while math_init.js begins with a rotating string/constant array (`const n7gIxM=[...]` shuffled by `WV8StW`), hex-only identifiers, and `with` blocks that defeat static parsing. A package that presents itself only as a prebuilt native binary has no legitimate reason to pull a separate JavaScript runtime and use it to execute an opaque, obfuscated sibling bundle at `npm install` time; the auto-executed code path is arbitrary and hidden from Node-resolvable static review. The Bun runtime is fetched from Bun's own official GitHub release (pinned to v1.3.13), so the runtime itself is legitimate; the harmful surface is the obfuscated math_init.js that runs under it on every install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
